items.description: Gianni Infantino est un dirigeant sportif né le 23 mars 1970. Il est actuellement président de la Fifa, et ce depuis le 26 février 2016. items.title: Al Ahli vs Al Nassr: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Al Ahli vs Al Nassr in the 2026-27 Saudi Pro League. Al Ahli host Al Nassr in a 2026-27 Saudi Pro League fixture that pits two sides coming off very different recent scorelines, with goals flying in at both ends over the past few weeks.
Al Ahli were beaten 6-1 by Al Shabab on October 30, a heavy loss that followed wins of 4-1 over Al Khaleej on October 23 and 3-2 over Al-Fayha on October 19. That run shows a team capable of scoring freely but also prone to conceding in bunches, and bouncing back quickly from the Al Shabab result matters a great deal for Marino Pušić’s group. A home game against a title rival is the sort of fixture that can either steady the ship or deepen the wobble.
Al Nassr arrive in much better form, having won 5-3 against Al Kholood on October 29 after previous victories of 3-1 over Al-Faisaly on October 23 and 1-0 against Neom SC on October 20. Three straight wins, each with goals involved except the Neom SC game, point to a team hitting a consistent attacking stride. Keeping that momentum intact on the road would send a strong signal to the rest of the league.
Al Ahli confirmed lineup
Marino Pušić sets Al Ahli up in a 4-2-3-1 with Édouard Mendy behind a back four of Saeed Baattia, Mohammed Sulaiman, Roger Ibañez and Abubacarr Sedi Kinteh. Artem Bondarenko and Eduard Spertsyan sit in front of that defense, screening for a attacking line of Valentin Atangana Edoa, Francisco Trincão and Wenderson Galeno behind lone striker Ivan Toney. There are no absences listed, so Pušić has his full projected group available, which will matter after conceding six goals in the last outing and needing more control in midfield.
Al Ahli confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Édouard Mendy, Saeed Baattia, Merih Demiral, Roger Ibañez, Saad Balobaid, Ziyad Al-Johani, Eduard Spertsyan, Valentin Atangana Edoa, Francisco Trincão, Ivan Toney, Wenderson Galeno. Coach: Marino Pušić.
Al Nassr confirmed lineup
Ange Postecoglou lines Al Nassr up in a 4-4-1-1, with Bento Krepski in goal protected by Nawaf Al-Boushail, Abdulelah Al Amri, Iñigo Martínez and Awad Aman. Ayman Yahya, Ângelo Gabriel, João Félix and Samu make up the midfield four, feeding Sadio Mané in support of Cristiano Ronaldo at the top of the shape. With no absences listed, Postecoglou can pick his strongest projected XI, and the Ronaldo-Mané pairing up front looks suited to exploiting a defense that has leaked goals recently.
Al Nassr confirmed starting XI (4-4-1-1): Bento Krepski, Nawaf Al-Boushail, Mohamed Simakan, Iñigo Martínez, Awad Aman, Abdullah Al-Hamdan, Ângelo Gabriel, João Félix, Samu, Abdullah Al-Khaibari, Cristiano Ronaldo. Coach: Ange Postecoglou.

items.description: A Javier Aguirre le esperan semanas importantes al frente del Valencia, con varios enfrentamientos ante rivales directos en la lucha por la permanencia. El técnico mexicano es consciente de que cada partido tiene su peso en una temporada en la que el equipo necesita sumar cuanto antes para salir de la zona de descenso, aunque recordó que la exigencia forma parte de su trabajo diario. “Me cuesta mucho hablar de mí mismo, del pasado y del futuro, uno se juega el turrón y el cargo cada semana. Estamos expuestos a la crítica, al análisis público y el que no entienda esto no sirve para el cargo. No sé la Liga que me juego, pero sé que es muy importante el partido de mañana”, afirmó en la previa del duelo ante el Rayo Vallecano.

items.title: José Alberto: "La Real es muy vertical, con velocidad, precisión y agresividad"
items.description: El entrenador del Racing Club de Santander, José Alberto López, defendió su apuesta por "jugar para ganar" y aseguró que esa mentalidad es la que pretende trasladar a su equipo en cada partido, también en el encuentro del domingo ante la Real Sociedad, en el que los cántabros buscarán volver a la senda de la victoria en los Campos de Sport de El Sardinero. "Pienso que jugar para ganar te da mucho más que jugar para no perder, esa es mi mentalidad y es lo que pretendemos", afirmó en la rueda de prensa previa al encuentro, aunque reconoció que en ocasiones firmaría un empate en los últimos minutos.

items.title: Luis Enrique entraîneur du PSG
items.description: Luis Enrique Martínez García, dit Luis Enrique, est un ancien footballeur international espagnol reconverti en entraîneur, né le 8 mai 1970 à Gijón. Ex-sélectionneur de l'équipe d'Espagne, il entraîne actuellement le Paris Saint-Germain. Il fait partie des rares joueurs à avoir joué à la fois pour le Real Madrid et pour le FC Barcelone, qu'il a également entraîné pendant trois saisons et avec qui il a remporté la Ligue des champions 2015.

items.title: Ousmane Dembélé
items.description: Ousmane Dembélé est un footballeur international français né à Vernon en 1997. Jeune surdoué formé en Normandie et au stade rennais, il explose à Dortmund avant de rejoindre le FC Barcelone pour pallier le départ de Neymar au PSG, c'est à l'époque le deuxième plus gros transfert de l'histoire du football. L'adaptation, gênée par les blessure, n'est pas simple pour l'ailier français, qui parvient tout de même à se faire une place en équipe de France dans le groupe qui devient champion du monde en 2018. Absent en 2020, il est de nouveau de la partie en 2022 et fait partie du 11 titulaire.

items.title: "Astiazarán y Folgado no van a poder estar y de Marchal y Dani Díaz sabremos mañana"
items.description: Jon Ansotegi quiere mantener la buena imagen ofrecida por el Sanse en los últimos partidos y dar continuidad a la racha de tres jornadas sin perder. "Tuvimos una mala racha, ahora llevamos tres partidos sin perder y creo que el equipo ha dado una buena imagen en ellos. Estamos con ganas de darle continuidad a la racha y obtener tres puntos. Hemos hecho una buena aproximación al partido. Tenemos todo para competir el partido y dar nuestra mejor versión", dijo el técnico realista, que analizó un poco lo que ha cambiado en el equipo de la racha mala a esta. "Han cambiado los resultados, eso lo primero. En esos 6 partidos perdidos, en alguno teníamos la sensación de no estar lejos de ganarlos pero por lo que sea se perdieron. Cuando algo no sale bien el equipo tiene que volver a lo básico, a ser difíciles para el rival, e hicimos eso. El equipo ha dado un pasito en eso, en general. Remangarnos más y ser conscientes de que habrá siempre momentos malos en los partidos, y esos sufrirlos, ser equipo y sacarlo adelante aprovechando los nuestros. El otro día hicimos muy buen primer tiempo, que lo dijo el rival también, y estás a nada de un 0-2 al descanso", añadió.

items.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
items.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegatedThe Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged.Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. items.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
items.description: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boysAfter three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. items.title: Antoine Griezmann claims an MLS award that slipped away from Lionel Messi in 2023
items.description:
Antoine Griezmann has earned an MLS honor that Lionel Messi came close to winning in 2023. 
Antoine Griezmann has barely settled into Major League Soccer, and he already has an individual honor to his name, one that even Lionel Messi did not win. The French forward was voted the league’s best newcomer after a standout first season with Orlando City.



MLS made it official this week: Griezmann is the 2026 Newcomer of the Year. The former Atletico Madrid forward arrived at Orlando City in March but did not take the field until July, and from then on his impact was immediate. He finished the regular season with 14 goals and eight assists, a club-best 22 goal contributions.



He needed only 15 games to reach 20 goal contributions, the second-fastest mark in league history, and he was involved in 32.9% of Orlando’s 63 goals, which helped the team reach the playoffs as the Eastern Conference’s No. 8 seed.



With 51.02% of the votes, he finished well ahead of Houston’s Guilherme (25.12%) and Sporting Kansas City’s Andre Luiz (6.19%), and he led in all three groups of voters: players, media and clubs.




The new guys lit up the league this year. 🔥The voters' choice? Antoine Griezmann. 🗳️ pic.twitter.com/0BZatgeSgr— Major League Soccer (@MLS) November 17, 2026




Messi came close to winning it in 2023



Messi will never have another chance to win this award, since it recognizes players in their first year in MLS, but he came close to taking it in 2023. The Argentine arrived at Inter Miami that summer and finished second in the voting with 27.28%, behind Atlanta United’s Giorgos Giakoumakis, who received 45.78%.


        


Messi did win the players’ vote that year, with 35.54%, narrowly ahead of Giakoumakis, who got 34.34%. But the media and club votes tilted the balance toward the Greek striker, who took the award, and Eduard Lowen of St. Louis City finished third with 15.44%.



With the playoffs about to begin, Griezmann will try to turn an award-winning debut into a deeper run with Orlando City, while Messi and Inter Miami arrive as defending champions. Their paths could keep crossing in the conversation, even if only one of them will have this particular trophy on the shelf.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement plans emerge as Real Madrid could welcome Portugal star back for special occasion
items.description:
Although the Portugal legend remains focused on his future with Al-Nassr, reports suggest discussions about a more fitting farewell are already taking shape, with some familiar faces potentially involved. 
Cristiano Ronaldo‘s international retirement has raised fresh questions about how one of soccer’s greatest careers will eventually come to an end. Although the Portugal legend remains focused on his future with Al-Nassr, reports suggest discussions about a more fitting farewell are already taking shape, with some familiar faces potentially involved.



The 41-year-old still has major ambitions before considering retirement from the game altogether. However, his departure from international soccer has left unfinished business, particularly after the difficult circumstances surrounding his final months with Portugal.



According to The Athletic, people close to Ronaldo say his immediate sporting priority is reaching 1,000 career goals. He reportedly has 985 goals to his name, leaving him 15 short of the historic milestone as he continues playing for Al-Nassr.



Ronaldo has previously indicated that he could consider retiring after the Saudi Pro League season next June. Beyond the goalscoring target, however, those familiar with his plans suggest he has relatively few other sporting ambitions before eventually bringing his playing career to a close.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Al Nassr celebrates a goal.



Portugal hopes to give its former captain proper send-off



Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5, 2026, ending a 23-year career with Portugal. He finished with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both men’s international records, while winning Euro 2016 and two Nations League titles.



His departure came after a difficult period involving head coach Jorge Jesus, with their disagreement over Ronaldo’s unused substitute appearance against Norway contributing to the breakdown in their relationship. The former captain’s last appearance came in September’s 1-0 victory over Wales, meaning he never received a proper farewell in front of Portugal supporters.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal.



The Athletic adds there is still hope on both sides that the situation can eventually be resolved. The report suggests that “in time, all sides are hopeful they can arrange a formal farewell game” to recognize Ronaldo’s contribution to Portuguese soccer, although “a little more time may be needed for the freshest of wounds to fully heal.”



Real Madrid could play role as well



Beyond a potential Portugal tribute, Ronaldo could receive a separate farewell involving some of his former clubs, with Real Madrid among those mentioned. Such an occasion would offer an opportunity to celebrate his achievements across club soccer before he eventually retires altogether, the report reveals.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Real Madrid CF holds the Ballon d’Or 2013



His connection with Real Madrid makes the possibility particularly significant. Ronaldo spent nine seasons at the Santiago Bernabéu between 2009 and 2018, scoring 451 goals in 438 appearances and becoming the club’s all-time leading goalscorer. He also helped Real Madrid win four Champions League titles, two La Liga championships and numerous other trophies. 



His contribution to the club’s historic European dominance cemented his place among its greatest-ever players. Ronaldo joined Real Madrid from Manchester United in 2009 for a then-world-record $103 million transfer fee. During his time in Spain, he won four Ballons d’Or and established several scoring records, including the remarkable 17-goal Champions League campaign in 2013-14.









His departure in 2018 brought an end to one of the most successful individual spells in the club’s history, as he moved to Juventus before later returning to Manchester United and eventually joining Al-Nassr. A farewell involving Los Blancos would therefore provide a fitting opportunity to celebrate the achievements that defined much of his career.

items.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insightLionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m.Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. items.title: Christian Pulisic reveals what Mauricio Pochettino told USMNT before Man Utd move and singles out what U.S. Soccer must demand from his successor
items.description:
The result secured another important achievement for the Americans, while Pulisic's outstanding performance provided a memorable moment in the Argentine coach's farewell. 
Christian Pulisic and Mauricio Pochettino ended their time together with the United States men’s national team on a high after a convincing victory over Haiti in Cincinnati. The result secured another important achievement for the Americans, while Pulisic’s outstanding performance provided a memorable moment in the Argentine coach’s farewell.



The Milan forward also reflected on the progress made during Pochettino’s tenure and the direction the national team should take next. With the former Tottenham and Chelsea manager preparing for a new challenge at Manchester United, attention is already turning towards the person who will replace him.



Pulisic opened the scoring in the 25th minute with an acrobatic bicycle kick after Weston McKennie delivered a cross towards the far post. The finish was particularly memorable because it was the first bicycle kick Pulisic had scored in his professional or international career. “I’d never scored a goal like that before. It was special. Weston crossed the ball, and it was really the only thing I could do, so I thought I had to give it a go. It was really nice to see the ball go in,” Pulisic said after the match.



The goal was his 36th for the United States, while McKennie later assisted 18-year-old Julian Hall for the second goal in the 43rd minute. The 2-0 victory completed an 8-0 aggregate win over Haiti, sending the United States into the Concacaf Nations League Finals scheduled for March 2027. The Americans also secured qualification for the 2027 Gold Cup and extended their winning run to six matches.



EVERY ANGLE OF THE PULISIC BICYCLE KICK 🎥 pic.twitter.com/jFSFZx5Wan— U.S. Soccer Men’s National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026



Pochettino finished his tenure with a record of 23 wins, two draws, and 12 defeats, having taken charge in October 2024. His departure was an emotional occasion, with the coach embracing his players and receiving a standing ovation from the crowd at TQL Stadium.



Play Country Roads. pic.twitter.com/gHgVmlIZ9J— U.S. Soccer Men’s National Team (@USMNT) November 18, 2026



Pulisic reveals Pochettino’s final message to the USMNT



Pulisic offered an insight into what the Argentine told the squad before leaving for England to take over at Manchester United. Rather than focusing on individual performances or immediate results, Pochettino’s farewell message centered on the culture and foundations built during his time with the national team.



“Simply that we have a really extraordinary culture. We’ve built something really special and have a bright future ahead of us. And to keep it going, letting the rest of the team support us,” Pulisic revealed.



Christian Pulisic on his bicycle kick, Pochettino, and Julian Hall pic.twitter.com/F3ITKV4yeR— TopBin90 (@Topbin90) November 18, 2026



The forward believes the United States has made meaningful progress under the former Paris Saint-Germain manager and should be confident about what lies ahead. “We’re in a good place. I mean, I think the team have improved. I think there’s a good culture within the group and I think we should be really excited about the future,” he added.



Pochettino also expressed confidence in the squad’s potential, pointing to the combination of experienced internationals and emerging young players. “I am sure that this group of players will achieve big things in the future. I have no doubt,” he told reporters.



Pulisic outlines what Pochettino’s successor must deliver



With Pochettino moving to Manchester United, U.S. Soccer must now find a manager capable of maintaining the progress made during his tenure. Pulisic acknowledged that the identity of the next coach matters, even though the players have no say in the appointment.



USMNT celebrate vs Mexico



“I mean, it’s not that it doesn’t matter. In the end, it’s not our choice as players. Whoever comes in, we hope they know how to make the most of the things we do very well and can lead us in a good direction,” he explained.



U.S. Soccer chief executive J.T. Batson has also highlighted the qualities the federation will prioritize when choosing a successor. Speaking before the Haiti match, Batson said the next appointment must care about youth development, the youth national team programs, relationships with clubs, and the wider success of the federation.

Sign up now!Although the millions of gamers who are pulling sickies would beg to differ, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI wasn’t the most exciting midnight launch involving a sprawling enterprise full of shady characters. Over in Zurich, the clock also struck 12 on the candidate deadline for next year’s Fifa presidential election, leaving those of us who have no interest in video games with our own chaotic, multi-billion-dollar sandbox where untouchable bosses bend the rules to suit themselves. While online carjackers are busy exploring a “most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world”, football’s real-life power brokers are gearing up for a March showdown in the actual city of Rabat.When I first saw the photo in yesterday’s Football Daily, I thought Mauricio Pochettino had opted for a short back and sides, presumably to pre-empt him tearing his luscious locks out in frustration at forthcoming poor results/terrible January transfer window/petulant sniping from sulky squad members. Then I realised he was in the back seat, all but entirely obscured by the rear-view mirror, in which he could perhaps see his sense of job satisfaction disappearing …” – Phil Taverner.That photo of Pochettino being chauffeured by a beefy driver answered one of my burning questions: what’s Ange Postecoglou doing these days?” – Mike Wilner (and others).This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. items.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
items.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quicklyIt’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it.But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio. From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

items.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
items.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficultyIn December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close.Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo’s former Portugal role comes into focus as Jorge Jesus makes strong Goncalo Ramos verdict with six-match argument
items.description:
The striker’s recent performances have brought fresh scrutiny, leaving the coach with questions to answer about his attacking options and the direction of the national team. 
Cristiano Ronaldo’s departure from Portugal has opened a new chapter for Goncalo Ramos, who has been given greater responsibility under Jorge Jesus during the Nations League campaign. However, the striker’s recent performances have brought fresh scrutiny, leaving the coach with questions to answer about his attacking options and the direction of the national team.



Ramos enjoyed an encouraging start after stepping into the spotlight, but his latest outings have been far less productive. With the Selecao preparing for the next stage of the competition, Jesus has offered his assessment of the forward’s development and his place in the squad.



Ramos became a regular starter after Ronaldo left the Portugal camp in October following a disagreement over playing time and team rules. The incident reportedly resulted in a 30-day suspension and a €255 fine from the Portuguese Soccer Federation’s Disciplinary Council, before Ronaldo announced his international retirement on November 5



The Milan striker initially responded well to the opportunity, scoring in three consecutive starts against Norway and Denmark while also providing an assist. He finished the Nations League group stage with three goals and one assist in six appearances, helping Portugal secure first place in Group A4 with 15 points.



Ramos scored the final goal



Ramos also attracted attention off the pitch after resharing a social media post describing him as “the best out-and-out striker” in Portuguese soccer. The message, originally shared by commentator Luís Freitas Lobo, was interpreted by some Ronaldo supporters as an indirect comparison with the former captain, although Ramos later deleted it.



Portugal’s November results increase the pressure



The striker’s promising run came to a halt during the November international break, when Portugal suffered a 4-1 defeat against Denmark before recovering with a 3-2 victory over Wales. Ramos started both matches but failed to score, registering no shots against either opponent before being substituted after 60 minutes in Cardiff.



His goal drought across club and international soccer had reached 661 minutes since October 18, according to the figures supplied in the reports. The contrast with his earlier contributions made his performances a talking point, particularly as he was now leading the attack following Ronaldo’s retirement.

Jorge Jesus’ players nevertheless finished top of their group and qualified for the Nations League quarter-finals. The result against Wales also allowed Jesus’ side to end the league phase on a positive note, despite Ramos having a quiet evening.



Jorge Jesus delivers his verdict on Goncalo Ramos



Jesus has defended his decision to continue trusting Ramos, pointing to the striker’s overall contribution rather than focusing exclusively on his latest appearances. The Portugal coach also highlighted how quickly the forward has developed and suggested there is still considerable room for improvement. “He is developing quickly and will continue to improve,” Jesus said, praising the progress Ramos has made.



The coach also believes the striker’s current level represents an important addition to Milan under manager Ruben Amorim. Jesus has known Ramos since the forward’s early days at Benfica, giving him a longer perspective on the player’s development. His assessment suggests that the recent scoring drought has not changed his belief in Ramos’ potential, even as competition for places in Portugal’s attack continues.









Ramos faces a defining period after Ronaldo’s retirement



Ramos’ overall Nations League numbers provide a more balanced picture of his first extended opportunity to lead Portugal’s attack. His three goals and one assist helped the national team finish first in Group A4, although his two November performances showed that maintaining that impact will be an important challenge.



Ronaldo’s retirement has inevitably changed the competition for attacking positions and leadership responsibilities within the squad. Ramos is among the players expected to benefit from the transition, but his place will continue to depend on performances and the demands of Jesus’ tactical approach. Portugal will discover its quarter-final opponent in the Nations League draw on November 20, with the knockout ties scheduled for March 2027.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni takes a subtle dig at Unai Simon after the goalkeeper ranked England above Argentina: ‘We beat them’
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni answered Unai Simon’s remark about England with a calm reply, though one phrase hinted at a message. 
A comment made by Spain goalkeeper Unai Simon in the wake of a painful defeat ended up reaching Argentina’s camp, and Lionel Scaloni chose to answer in a calm but pointed way.



The goalkeeper was speaking after Spain lost 3-2 to England in Madrid on Nov. 15, a result that ended the world champions’ long unbeaten run and handed England first place in the group.



“In the end, we knew the streak would end at some point,” he said. “England was a team against which that could happen because, in my opinion, I think it’s the second-best team in the world. Even if the FIFA ranking doesn’t say so, I think its level is comparable to ours, and it hurts to lose”. Since Argentina occupies second place in that list, with Spain first and England fourth, his words read as a jab at the Albiceleste.



The Argentine coach responded with great respect, but at the end of his message he also seemed to leave a subtle hint in reply to Simon’s words. “He thinks England is a great team, which it is. It’s an incredible team that we beat. But it’s his opinion and it has to be respected,” Scaloni said.



Unai Simón, en DAZN: "Inglaterra es la segunda mejor selección del mundo. Aunque el ranking de la FIFA no lo diga"."Tienen un nivel similar al nuestro". https://t.co/kBEdekMj5W pic.twitter.com/fuSagZjJi2— Albert Ortega (@AlbertOrtegaES1) November 16, 2026 



The reference points to Argentina’s 2-1 comeback against England in the World Cup semifinal in July, when Enzo Fernandez and Lautaro Martinez scored late after Anthony Gordon had given England the lead.



How the FIFA ranking looks after the international window


        


Spain remains at the head of the FIFA ranking with 2,004.48 points, followed by Argentina in second place with 1,966.13. Argentina held its position after the November window, which included a 2-1 loss to Uruguay and the 7-0 rout of Costa Rica. France follows in third place with 1,950.82 and England completes the top four with 1,938.90, a group that sits well clear of the rest of the table.



Behind them, the biggest movement came from Morocco, which climbed two places to fifth with 1,809.37 points, the best position in its history. Portugal slipped one spot to sixth with 1,801.28, and Brazil also fell one place to seventh with 1,800.91.



For now, the debate remains in the realm of words, since the pitch will have the final say. Argentina next takes the field in the March 22-30 window, while Spain and England will meet again in the Nations League spotlight, and the table, updated next on Dec. 16, will keep measuring who really sits where.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo holds the UEFA Euro records, but Jorge Jesus has a very different view of the competition compared to Nations League
items.description:
After a dramatic victory over Wales secured Portugal's place at the top of its Nations League group, the manager has made his position clear on the challenges awaiting his team and the competition's place in European soccer. 
Cristiano Ronaldo helped Portugal establish itself among Europe’s most successful national teams, while Jorge Jesus is now attempting to guide the country into a new chapter following the legendary forward’s international retirement. After a dramatic victory over Wales secured Portugal’s place at the top of its Nations League group, the manager has made his position clear on the challenges awaiting his team and the competition’s place in European soccer.



Jesus believes Portugal has every reason to approach the upcoming knockout stage with confidence, despite questions surrounding its recent performances. His latest comments have also reignited a debate about the relative difficulty of Europe’s two major international tournaments.



Portugal secured a 3-2 victory over Wales in Cardiff, bouncing back from a heavy 4-1 home defeat to Denmark in its previous Nations League fixture. The result ensured that Jesus‘ side finished top of Group A4 with 15 points from six matches, recording five victories and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.



Jesus insists Portugal should fear nobody



The result came at an important moment for Jesus, whose team had faced criticism following its disappointing performance against Denmark. The manager acknowledged that the victory was important because doubts were already emerging about the progress Portugal had made during his tenure. “It was good to win because people were already starting to cast doubt on what we have achieved here,” Jesus explained, according to A Bola.









The Portuguese manager also dismissed concerns about the identity of Portugal’s next opponent, insisting that his team should approach the quarter-finals without fear. With potential opponents including Spain, Belgium and the Netherlands, Jesus made clear that he has no particular preference for the draw.



“Whatever comes out in the draw is fine. I’m not afraid of anyone, and let the others be afraid of Portugal,” he said. He also highlighted the country’s previous success, adding that Portugal remains a contender because it has already won the competition twice.



Jesus makes bold Nations League versus Euro comparison



However, Jesus made his most striking statement when discussing the difficulty of the Nations League compared with the European Championship. The 72-year-old believes the format of the Nations League exposes teams to stronger opposition much earlier in the competition.



“This Nations League is stronger than the European Championship. In the group stage, you play against great European teams. In the European Championship, you play against teams that have nothing to do with the Nations League,” he declared. His argument centers on the concentration of established European sides in League A, where the strongest national teams regularly face each other during the group stage.









The European Championship, by comparison, includes a wider range of teams, meaning some group-stage fixtures involve nations with considerably different levels of experience and quality. Jesus also acknowledged that soccer can produce unexpected results regardless of reputation. “Sometimes the strong become weaker, and the weaker become stronger,” he added.



Ronaldo and Portugal’s European Championship and Nations League success



Portugal’s history in both competitions provides important context for Jesus’s confidence. The national team won its first European Championship in 2016, defeating hosts France 1-0 after extra time, with Ronaldo captaining the side despite being forced off through injury during the final.



Cristiano Ronaldo of Portugal holds the Euro 2016 trophy



Ronaldo remains central to the Selecao’s international legacy, finishing his career with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both national records. He also helped the country secure its first Nations League title in 2019, when Portugal defeated the Netherlands 1-0 in the final.

Portugal subsequently added a second Nations League trophy in 2025, beating Spain on penalties after a 2-2 draw in the final. That success made it the first nation to win the competition twice, giving Jesus a strong foundation for his belief that his current team can challenge for another title.

items.title: Lionel Messi’s mother reportedly found Argentina’s next star in Nico Paz: ‘You are my son’s successor’
items.description:
Since Lionel Messi stepped away from the national team, the question of who will lead Argentina into the next era has hovered over every match. Nico Paz keeps appearing in that conversation, and a story from his own family now adds an emotional piece to it. Paz scored a brace in Argentina’s 7-0 rout of […] 
Since Lionel Messi stepped away from the national team, the question of who will lead Argentina into the next era has hovered over every match. Nico Paz keeps appearing in that conversation, and a story from his own family now adds an emotional piece to it.



Paz scored a brace in Argentina’s 7-0 rout of Costa Rica in a friendly played at the Kempes stadium in Cordoba on Tuesday, the final match of the national team’s year. Despite playing only the first half, he was one of the standout players of the night. Shortly afterward, his uncle, Fabian Paz, spoke on Argentina’s Radio La Red and revealed a private exchange between the Como midfielder and Celia Cuccittini, Messi’s mother.



According to the relative, it happened after Messi’s farewell on Oct. 6, a 3-0 win over Benin at the Monumental in which Nico shared the pitch with him. When the midfielder left the locker room, he found Cuccittini in tears, went over to greet her since they already knew each other, and she took his hand and told him: “You are my son’s successor”. Fabian Paz said the player came out in shock, and that Nico himself described the moment as something incredible.



The uncle insisted that his nephew does not walk around with that label. “He doesn’t have it in his head to be Messi’s successor,” he said, adding that for Nico, getting to know Messi and play alongside him was like touching the sky.




𝐉𝐮𝐬𝐭 𝐍𝐢𝐜𝐨 😮‍💨 pic.twitter.com/nufxHll5y8— Selección Argentina in English (@AFASeleccionEN) November 17, 2026




Paz has contributed to six goals in the last five games, and Lionel Scaloni said after the Costa Rica match that the youngster “can give even more” and that there are reasons for optimism about the new generation.



Nico Paz downplays talk of inheriting Messi’s No. 10


        


Nico Paz was the best player on the pitch in Cordoba despite playing only the first half, and he used the moment after the final whistle to reflect on his first full year with the national team. Speaking to TyC Sports, he said: “Representing this shirt is the greatest thing, especially on days like this, when they’ve given us so much affection”.



He then explained how he sees his own progress. “I think I’m improving, having fun on the field, and with the quality of players we have, incredible quality, it becomes easier. It’s incredible to be able to play on this team,” the Como midfielder continued.



Then came the question the whole country is asking: whether he sees himself taking over the No. 10 that Messi left vacant. Paz did not take the bait. “I don’t think about the jersey number; I play because I love soccer and what it creates in people. I only think about enjoying it, I want to keep enjoying playing,” he concluded.



The reply fits the tone he has kept all along, and it came after a night in which Argentina closed its year with seven goals, two each from Paz, Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono, plus one from Alexis Mac Allister.



The next chance to see the team will come in the FIFA window of March 22-30, 2027, when it is expected to play one or two friendlies against rivals that have not yet been defined, and where it will become clear whether the legendary No. 10 shirt remains unused or finds a new owner.

items.title: Joao Cancelo and Bruno Fernandes’ armband moment sparks controversy after Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal retirement
items.description:
A brief exchange after Portugal’s win over Wales has put Joao Cancelo, Bruno Fernandes and Cristiano Ronaldo at the center of attention. 
Portugal’s first victory since Cristiano Ronaldo stepped away from the national team came with an unexpected sequel off the pitch. A brief exchange between two of the squad’s leading figures, captured by television cameras once the match was over, has been picked apart by supporters ever since.



The moment took place in Cardiff on Tuesday, after Portugal edged Wales 3-2 in the Nations League. Goals from Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto and Carlos Forbs answered strikes by David Brooks and Sorba Thomas, and the result lifted Jorge Jesus’ side to the top of its group.



With Bernardo Silva, the new permanent captain, absent from the squad, Fernandes wore the armband and passed it to Joao Cancelo when he was substituted late in the match.



In footage broadcast on Sport TV after the final whistle, Fernandes pointed toward Cancelo and appeared to say “record him” to the cameraman. The full-back then pointed to the captain’s armband on his sleeve and said, “Film the boss,” according to Portuguese media, in what looked like a light-hearted moment.



pic.twitter.com/FHYsKdlQes— Goncalitosvid (@Goncalitosvid) November 18, 2026 



That has not stopped a portion of Ronaldo’s followers from reading it as a mockery. The timing explains part of the reaction, since the forward announced his international retirement on Nov. 5 after 234 appearances and 146 goals, having worn the armband for around two decades.



Several fans on X criticized both players and suggested the joke was aimed at Cristiano, while others simply saw an innocent bit of banter after a win that eased the sting of the 4-1 loss to Denmark.


        


Portugal secure a place in the Nations League quarter-finals



The win in Cardiff left Portugal at the top of their group, and as group winners, the reigning champions will be seeded in the draw for the quarter-finals, scheduled for Nov. 20 at UEFA’s headquarters. 



Teams from the same group cannot meet, so Norway is ruled out as a potential opponent, and Jorge Jesus’ side will be paired with one of the runners-up from the other three groups.



The possible rivals are Belgium, the Netherlands and Spain. The tie will be played over two legs, with first legs between March 25 and 27 and second legs between March 28 and 30, 2027.



For a group still adjusting to life without its all-time leading scorer, the draw will offer a first look at the road ahead. Whatever the outcome, the next international window in March will show whether the armband debate fades away or stays part of the conversation.

items.title: Lionel Messi earns Globe Soccer Awards nomination for Best Men’s Player, while Cristiano Ronaldo is left out again
items.description:
Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo head into the Globe Soccer Awards with very different outcomes. 
The Globe Soccer Awards have unveiled the shortlist for their 2026 edition, and the rivalry between Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, the two players who defined an era, is once again part of the conversation. The best men’s player category has a familiar name returning and a notable absence, and the contrast says a lot about where each of them stands as the awards head to Dubai.



The Argentine forward is among the nominees, after a season in which he won his second straight MLS Golden Boot with 26 goals and 17 assists and led Inter Miami to the playoffs. Ronaldo, on the other hand, is not on the list of the main category, although he remains nominated for Best Middle East Player, an award he won last year.



Ousmane Dembele, Kylian Mbappe, Harry Kane and Lamine Yamal are also among the contenders, and the winners will be announced on Dec. 28 in Dubai, with public voting open until Nov. 30.



The history of the awards explains why the names carry weight. Ronaldo is the most decorated player in the history of the Best Player category, with six wins in 2011, 2014, 2016, 2017, 2018 and 2019, and he has also received other honors, including the Player of the Century award for 2001-2020. Messi, in contrast, has won the Best Player award only once, in 2015, after a season in which he lifted the Champions League with Barcelona.




The nominees for Best Men's Player at the 2026 BEYOND Developments GLOBE SOCCER AwardsCongratulations to all the nominees.Vote for your finalists via the link in bio, at https://t.co/ZFEV3AEjn3, or on the Globe Soccer App. pic.twitter.com/upBO8mZFQ0— Globe Soccer Awards (@Globe_Soccer) November 18, 2026




Last year, neither of them was among the nominees for the top prize. Ronaldo was only nominated in the Middle East category, which he went on to win, while Messi did not appear in any category despite his MLS numbers, and Dembele ended up winning the Best Men’s Player award.



Full list of nominees for Best Men’s Player



Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid)Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona)Ousmane Dembele (Paris Saint-Germain)Federico Dimarco (Inter Milan)Desire Doue (Paris Saint-Germain)Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United)Erling Haaland (Manchester City)Achraf Hakimi (Paris Saint-Germain)Harry Kane (Bayern Munich)Khvicha Kvaratskhelia (Paris Saint-Germain)Lautaro Martinez (Inter Milan)Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid)Lionel Messi (Inter Miami)Nuno Mendes (Paris Saint-Germain)Joao Neves (Paris Saint-Germain)Michael Olise (Bayern Munich)Raphinha (Barcelona)Declan Rice (Arsenal)Rodri (Manchester City)Fabian Ruiz (Paris Saint-Germain)Bukayo Saka (Arsenal)William Saliba (Arsenal)Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool)Vinicius Jr. (Real Madrid)Vitinha (Paris Saint-Germain)Lamine Yamal (Barcelona)



With voting open until Nov. 30, Messi will try to add a second Globe Soccer Best Player trophy to the one he won in 2015, in a field where he is the only nominee outside Europe, while Ronaldo waits on the Best Middle East Player award. The verdict in Dubai on Dec. 28 will add one more chapter to a rivalry that continues even after both stepped away from international soccer.

items.title: Argentina holds firm while Portugal drops a spot in the first FIFA ranking without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo
items.description:
Argentina and Portugal take their first steps without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, and the latest FIFA ranking shows that only one of them kept its place. 
The first FIFA ranking after the first international window without Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo is out, and it shows two national teams reacting differently to life without their biggest stars. Both Argentina and Portugal suffered a defeat in the November break, but the effect on the table was not the same for each.



Argentina remains in second place with 1,966.13 points, behind only Spain, which leads with 2,004.48. The Albiceleste lost 2-1 to Uruguay in its first match since Messi’s retirement, but it bounced back with a 7-0 win over Costa Rica to close the year, and it stays ahead of France (1,950.82) and England (1,938.90).



Portugal was less fortunate. The team dropped from fifth to sixth place with 1,801.28 points, after a 4-1 home loss to Denmark in a match that was supposed to honor Ronaldo’s retirement, but finished as the heaviest home defeat the team has suffered in more than a century.



It recovered with a 3-2 win over Wales to finish first in its Nations League group, but that was not enough to hold its spot, as Morocco climbed two places to fifth with 1,809.37 points, its highest position ever. Brazil also slipped one place, to seventh, with 1,800.91 points, only 0.37 behind the Portuguese.



FIFA Rankings. (inside.fifa.com)



What’s next for Argentina and Portugal after the ranking update



The next ranking update will arrive on Dec. 16, but it is unlikely to bring changes at the top of the table, since national teams will not play again until the first FIFA window of 2027, set for March 22-30. That means the positions of Argentina and Portugal could stay as they are for months, with both teams closing the year in places that reflect very different roads.


        


Argentina will return to action in March with one or two friendlies, as FIFA allows a maximum of two matches in that window and the federation has not yet started negotiations with any opponent.



European teams will be busy with the Nations League, so the Albiceleste would likely face rivals from other confederations. Portugal, for its part, will go back to the Nations League quarterfinals, and both Lionel Scaloni and Jorge Jesus will use the time to keep building squads without Messi and Ronaldo.

items.title: Mexico vs Jamaica: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Mexico vs Jamaica in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Mexico host Jamaica in the Concacaf Nations League just days after the two sides met in a game that swung the wrong way for the hosts, and this rematch carries an obvious edge.
Mexico come into this one off a 2-3 loss to Jamaica on November 15, a result that saw them concede three goals at home and hand their rival a measure of belief heading into the return fixture. There is no earlier form listed beyond that defeat, which leaves Rafael Márquez’s side with little recent cushion to point to. A response is needed simply to steady the ship after that setback.
Jamaica arrive in good shape, having beaten Mexico 3-2 on November 15 before that they drew 1-1 with Honduras on October 6. Back to back results without a loss give Rudolph Speid’s group genuine confidence going into Mexican territory. A strong showing here would confirm Jamaica as a real threat in this Nations League cycle rather than a one-off upset side.
Mexico confirmed lineup
Márquez sends out a 4-3-3 built around Raúl Rangel in goal behind a back four of Rodrigo Huescas, Mateo Chávez, Israel Reyes and Jesús Orozco. Érik Lira anchors midfield alongside Álvaro Fidalgo, with Gilberto Mora given license to push forward from deep. Up top, Jesús Corona and Roberto Alvarado flank Julián Quiñones, giving Mexico width and pace to work with. There are no absences listed, so this looks close to a first-choice group tasked with avoiding a second straight loss to Jamaica.
Mexico confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Raúl Rangel, Rodrigo Huescas, Mateo Chávez, Érik Lira, Israel Reyes, Jesús Orozco, Gilberto Mora, Álvaro Fidalgo, Jesús Corona, Roberto Alvarado, Julián Quiñones. Coach: Rafael Márquez.
Jamaica confirmed lineup
Speid sticks with a 3-4-3, with Jahmali Waite in goal protected by Kyle Ming, Ronaldo Webster and Miguel Freckleton across the back. Richard King and Joël Latibeaudiere provide the central midfield platform, while Karoy Anderson and Courtney Clarke work the flanks in the four-man line. Javon East, Kaheim Dixon and Renaldo Cephas form the front three, the same attacking trio that did the damage in the last meeting. With no absences reported, Jamaica field a settled group looking to build on their recent win over this same opponent.
Jamaica confirmed starting XI (3-4-3): Jahmali Waite, Kyle Ming, Ronaldo Webster, Miguel Freckleton, Richard King, Joël Latibeaudiere, Karoy Anderson, Courtney Clarke, Javon East, Kaheim Dixon, Renaldo Cephas. Coach: Rudolph Speid.

items.title: Luis Suarez reveals how he sees his retirement alongside Lionel Messi, although it may not happen together
items.description:
Luis Suarez shared how he imagines the end of his career next to his longtime friend, but his answer suggests the finish line might not look the way many expect. 
Few friendships in soccer have lasted as long as the one between Luis Suarez and Lionel Messi, who first shared a dressing room at Barcelona and now do so again at Inter Miami.



With both in the final stretch of their careers, the question of how it will all end is starting to come up more and more, and Suarez gave his view on it in an interview with Catalunya Radio’s “Tot Costa” program.



The Uruguayan forward began by explaining that there is no set date and that the decision depends on the desire to keep competing. “It’s difficult, but well… As long as we keep having fun, enjoying ourselves and keep that competitive edge of wanting to win, of wanting to achieve things, neither he nor I nor everyone who has that ambition to keep achieving is going to stop,” he said.



Then came the part that points in another direction. Suarez imagined a moment in the future when their paths could split, because Messi, in his view, still has too much energy to stop. “There will come a time when he has so much energy, so much desire to keep playing that at some point I’m going to tell him: friend, everything is fine, you keep going, but I’ve come this far,” he explained with a laugh.



Lionel Messi and Luiz Suarez of Inter Miami. (Getty Images)



For now, he made it clear that both feel well. “As long as we’re fine, we’re happy, we’re enjoying ourselves and we look good physically, which is what people like, because one thing is to be there just to be there and another is to look good. On a personal level, I feel good, Leo is also fine, and that helps a lot,” Suarez said.



The forward, 39, has 17 goals and 8 assists in 32 matches this regular season, and his contract with Inter Miami expires at the end of the year, although he said talks to continue are underway.


        


Messi shows no signs of slowing down



While Suarez talks about the end of the road, Messi’s numbers say the Argentine is far from it. At 39, he led Inter Miami to the playoffs, with the team finishing second in the Eastern Conference, and closed the regular season with 26 goals and 17 assists, the best marks in the league in goals and in goal contributions (43). That earned him his second consecutive Golden Boot, which makes him the first player in MLS history to win it in back-to-back seasons.



Now he is also in the running for another record. Messi, who won the MVP award in 2024 and 2025, is one of five finalists for 2026 and is seen as the front-runner to become the first three-time winner in a row.



With numbers like these, it is easy to see why Suarez does not picture Messi stepping away anytime soon. Whether the two end up retiring together or not, the Argentine still has plenty to say on the pitch, starting with the playoffs, where Inter Miami will try to go for another title.

items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Argentina vs Costa Rica in a 2026 international friendly game. Argentina host Costa Rica in a 2026 international friendly that pits a World Cup winner’s squad against a Costa Rica side looking to find its footing ahead of next year.
Argentina come into this one off a 1-2 loss to Uruguay on November 13, a result that snapped a strong run that included a 3-0 win over Benin on October 6 and a 7-0 rout of Burkina Faso two days before that. The gap between those lopsided wins and the defeat to Uruguay shows how much this Argentina squad can vary depending on personnel and opponent. A clean performance here would settle any lingering questions from that Uruguay setback.
Costa Rica arrive having lost 0-2 to Ecuador on November 14, their most recent outing on record. That result leaves Bryan Ruiz’s side searching for answers heading into this friendly. A positive showing against a team of Argentina’s caliber would mean far more than the scoreline alone.
Argentina confirmed lineup
Lionel Scaloni sends out a 4-3-3 built around Enzo Fernández and Alexis Mac Allister in midfield, with Máximo Perrone also in the engine room to help control possession. Julián Alvarez and Nico Paz support Gianluca Prestianni up front, giving Argentina pace and movement across the frontline. At the back, Emiliano Martínez starts in goal behind a line of Agustín Giay, Román Vega, Lisandro Martínez and Facundo Medina. There are no absences listed for Argentina, so Scaloni has his full group of selected players to work with.
Argentina confirmed starting XI (4-3-3): Emiliano Martínez, Agustín Giay, Román Vega, Máximo Perrone, Lisandro Martínez, Facundo Medina, Enzo Fernández, Alexis Mac Allister, Julián Alvarez, Nico Paz, Gianluca Prestianni. Coach: Lionel Scaloni.
Costa Rica confirmed lineup
Bryan Ruiz lines Costa Rica up in a 4-1-4-1, with Celso Borges holding in front of the back four to shield Francisco Calvo, Juan Vargas, Kenyel Michel and Gerald Taylor. Andrey Soto, Carlos Mora, Aarón Salazar and Josimar Méndez make up a busy midfield four tasked with supporting lone striker Manfred Ugalde. Patrick Sequeira starts in goal behind that setup. Costa Rica have no absences listed, meaning Ruiz can call on his intended group against a tough Argentina side.

items.title: Al Nassr reportedly eyeing a historic father-son moment with Cristiano Ronaldo and Cristiano Jr
items.description:
Al Nassr is reportedly exploring a special scenario for Cristiano Ronaldo and his teenage son, one that would add a new chapter to the veteran forward’s career. 
Cristiano Ronaldo has spent more than two decades chasing records and trophies, but a different kind of milestone could be waiting for him in Saudi Arabia. After closing his international career with Portugal, the forward may still have one more special moment to live, this time at club level.



Al Nassr is reportedly working so that Ronaldo and his son can play together with the first team in 2027, according to Saudi journalist Tariq Al-Nofal. The club had already been linked to that idea in April, when Saudi outlet Al Wiam reported that it was considering inviting Cristiano Jr. to train with the senior squad next season, a plan that now appears to be getting closer.



The report arrives at a moment of growth for the young forward. The 16-year-old has stood out in Al Nassr’s youth ranks and has earned a place with Portugal’s youth national teams.



His rise reached a new stage shortly after his father’s retirement from Portugal, as he made his debut with the under-17 team, coming off the bench in the 73rd minute of a Euro 2027 qualifier against Andorra.



🚨| Cristiano Ronaldo Jr. delivers an amazing performance for Portugal U17! 🇵🇹🔥He’s clearly following in his father’s footsteps. 🐐 pic.twitter.com/ccwawoyA99— Kalshi EPL (@KalshiEPL) November 12, 2026 



Ronaldo, 41, is under contract with Al Nassr until June 2027, the same month in which Cristiano Jr. turns 17, so the timing of any shared appearance would depend on the teenager’s development and on the club’s sporting decisions in the coming months.



The plan could also serve Al Nassr beyond the pitch: with his contract nearing its end, the prospect of playing alongside his son could become a strong argument for convincing Ronaldo to extend his stay in Saudi Arabia.


        


Could Lionel Messi share the pitch with his son too?



The idea inevitably raises a question about Lionel Messi, who could be next in line for a similar scene. His eldest son, Thiago, turned 14 on Nov. 2 and plays for Inter Miami’s under-14 team, with which he won the MIC Football Punta Cana tournament in June.



The age gap also makes the comparison different: Thiago is two years younger than Cristiano Jr., so any chance of a father-son appearance for Messi would be further away and would depend on how long the Argentine, 39, continues playing and on how the teenager develops at the youth level.



For now, only Ronaldo’s case has emerged as a real possibility, since there are no reports of a similar plan for Messi and his son. Even so, the idea remains a report without official confirmation, and whether it becomes reality will depend on time, on Cristiano Jr.’s progress and on a decision from Ronaldo himself about how long he wants to keep playing.

items.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have company as Harry Kane joins elite Ballon d’Or list with goal against Spain
items.description:
The England captain's latest achievement puts him alongside some of the game's biggest legends, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, following a dramatic night in Madrid. 
Harry Kane has added his name to another exclusive chapter in soccer history after a memorable performance against Spain. The England captain’s latest achievement puts him alongside some of the game’s biggest legends, including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi, following a dramatic night in Madrid.



England claimed a 3-2 victory over Spain in the UEFA Nations League last Sunday, ending the reigning world champions’ remarkable unbeaten run. Kane played a decisive role, scoring from the penalty spot just before half-time to give Thomas Tuchel’s side the lead.



Thomas Tuchel’s players started brightly at the Metropolitano Stadium, pressing La Roja aggressively and preventing the home side from finding its usual rhythm. Kane won a penalty after being fouled by Pau Cubarsi and calmly converted it in the final moments of the first half, registering his 93rd international goal for England.



The visitors carried their momentum into the second half, with Ezri Konsa doubling the lead before Ben White made it 3-0 after a well-worked attacking move involving Jude Bellingham. England appeared to be heading towards a comfortable victory, but the match took a dramatic turn when Elliot Anderson was sent off for denying Lamine Yamal a goalscoring opportunity.









Spain took advantage of its numerical superiority, with Mikel Oyarzabal converting the resulting penalty before Nico Williams made it 3-2. However, James Trafford produced crucial saves late in the match to help England hold on and secure first place in its Nations League group.



Kane joins Messi and Ronaldo



Beyond the result, Kane’s goal carried a significant individual milestone. Soccer statistician MisterChip has revealed that the Bayern striker became the fifth reigning Ballon d’Or winner to score against Spain.



The list stretches back to 1984, when Michel Platini scored against Spain in the European Championship final. Roberto Baggio followed in the 1994 World Cup quarter-final, before Lionel Messi found the net against La Roja in a friendly in September 2010.



Harry Kane of England scores from the penalty spot against Spain



Cristiano Ronaldo became the fourth player to achieve the feat when he scored a hat-trick against Spain at the 2018 World Cup, with Kane now completing the exclusive group after his Nations League penalty. The five players and their respective matches are:



DatePlayerCountryCompetition27.06.1984Michel PlatiniFranceEuro final09.07.1994Roberto BaggioItalyWorld Cup quarter-final07.09.2010Lionel MessiArgentinaFriendly15.06.2018Cristiano RonaldoPortugalWorld Cup group stage (hat-trick)15.11.2026Harry KaneEnglandNations League group stageReigning Ballon d’Or winners to score against Spain



Kane’s inclusion adds another remarkable achievement to a career that has already seen him become England’s all-time leading goalscorer. He also joins Ronaldo and Messi in a statistic that highlights how rarely the reigning Ballon d’Or winner manages to score against Spain.

items.title: Why is Cristiano Ronaldo not playing for Portugal vs Wales in 2026-27 UEFA Nations League Matchday 6?
items.description:
Portugal faces Wales without Cristiano Ronaldo, following a heavy defeat suffered against Denmark. 
Portugal closes its Nations League group stage on Tuesday against Wales at Cardiff City Stadium, and the team sheet once again does not include the name Cristiano Ronaldo.



The reason for Ronaldo’s absence is that he is no longer part of the national team. The 41-year-old retired from international soccer on Nov. 5, ending a run of 234 appearances and 146 goals, both all-time records for his country and the world.



What is new is how Portugal got here. The team was beaten 4-1 by Denmark in Braga on Saturday, in a night that was supposed to honor Ronaldo and instead turned into the heaviest home defeat the team has suffered in more than a century.



Denmark was 4-0 up before Bernardo Silva scored a late goal, and Jesus took responsibility afterward. “If the team couldn’t do it, it has to do with my instructions,” the coach said. When asked if he misses Ronaldo, he replied: “How can I miss him when he is no longer in the national team?”




Fechar a fase de grupos com uma 𝙫𝙞𝙩𝙤́𝙧𝙞𝙖. ☝️🇵🇹 #NationsLeague pic.twitter.com/XdlwjDhxIT— Portugal (@selecaoportugal) November 17, 2026




The atmosphere in Braga reflected a mix of nostalgia and frustration. As parts of the crowd began to leave before the final whistle, some supporters chanted Ronaldo’s name, a sign that the farewell was still fresh even though the team failed to deliver on the pitch. 



Jesus acknowledged that feeling but made it clear that the page has been turned. “People miss him and have not forgotten what Cristiano did for 23 years with the national team, but there is no going back on the matter,” he said.


        


What is at stake for Portugal after the loss to Denmark



Even after the heavy defeat, Portugal’s situation is far from critical. The team had already booked a place in the quarterfinals thanks to four straight wins to open the campaign, so what remains in play is finishing at the top of Group A4. 



A point in Cardiff would be enough to secure it, while a slip could open the door for Denmark, which would pass Portugal by beating Norway on the same night.



The task will not be simple for Jesus, who has to rebuild his lineup with several names missing. Ruben Dias and Joao Palhinha are serving suspensions, and Bernardo Silva was ruled out as unfit after scoring Portugal’s lone goal against Denmark.



Portugal now has a chance to answer in Cardiff, in a match that can reset its direction after a tough week. With Ronaldo already gone from the national team, Jesus needs a response from his players to close the group stage as a winner.

items.title: Wales vs Portugal: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the projected lineups for Wales vs Portugal in the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League. Wales host Portugal at a stage of this Nations League campaign where both sides are still searching for answers on defense, and that shared problem should shape how this one is played.
Wales come into this match on the back of two straight defeats, falling 1-3 to Norway on November 14 after a 0-1 loss to Denmark back on October 4. The goals have dried up and the results have followed a similar pattern of narrow or lopsided losses. A result here matters for Craig Bellamy’s side simply to stop the losing run before it becomes a longer slide.
Portugal arrive having split their last two outings, beaten 1-4 by Denmark on November 14 just weeks after edging Norway 2-1 on October 4. That Denmark scoreline stands out as a heavy defeat for a squad of this quality, and it puts extra weight on how Jorge Jesus sets his team up here. A win would steady things after that result and keep Portugal’s campaign on track.
Wales confirmed lineup
Bellamy sets Wales up in a 4-4-2 with Karl Darlow behind a back line of Connor Roberts, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies and Jay DaSilva. The midfield pairing of Daniel James and Rubin Colwill on the flanks alongside Brennan Johnson, Lewis Koumas and Harry Wilson is built to supply the front two, with Liam Cullen leading the line. There are no listed absences, so this looks like the strongest group Bellamy has available, and the shape suggests Wales will look to get numbers forward quickly rather than sit back against a stronger side.
Wales confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Danny Ward, Connor Roberts, Jay Dasilva, David Brooks, Joe Rodon, Ben Davies, Daniel James, Josh Sheehan, Rubin Colwill, Harry Wilson, Sorba Thomas. Coach: Craig Bellamy.
Portugal confirmed lineup
Jesus goes with a 4-2-3-1, with Diogo Costa in goal and a back four of Diogo Dalot, Renato Veiga, António Silva and João Cancelo. Rúben Neves and Vítor Vitinha sit as the double pivot, screening for an attacking trio of Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto and João Félix behind lone striker Gonçalo Ramos. With no absences listed, Portugal field a full-strength XI, and the balance between Neves and Vitinha should let Fernandes push forward and link with Félix and Ramos in the final third.
Portugal confirmed starting XI (4-2-3-1): Diogo Costa, Diogo Dalot, João Cancelo, Vitinha, António Silva, Renato Veiga, Trincão, João Neves, Gonçalo Ramos, Bruno Fernandes, Pedro Neto. Coach: Jorge Fernando Pinheiro de Jesus.

items.title: Antoine Griezmann pays tribute to Cristiano Ronaldo: ‘What he has done for Portugal is historic’
items.description:
Antoine Griezmann has shared an emotional message for Cristiano Ronaldo, a longtime rival who he says leaves a huge void in Portugal. 
Antoine Griezmann has joined the long list of voices reacting to Cristiano Ronaldo’s retirement from international football, and his words carry the weight of someone who spent years competing against him.



The Frenchman shared his thoughts during a press conference with Orlando City, where he looked back on what the Portuguese star meant to the game, admitting that the news hit him. “I am sad about Cristiano’s retirement. He is an absolute legend, a machine when it comes to working, scoring goals and winning,” he told reporters.



His praise then focused on Ronaldo’s impact on his country, along with the void he leaves behind. “I really enjoyed playing against him, and the truth is that what he has done for Portugal is historic. He will be very difficult to replace,” Griezmann added.



Ronaldo brought his international career to an end on Nov. 5, when he decided to step aside amid tensions with head coach Jorge Jesus. The Portuguese legend leaves behind impressive numbers, with 234 appearances and 146 goals, both world records at the national team level.



🐐🔥 CRISTIANO RONALDO HAS A HIGH-PROFILE ADMIRER!🇫🇷⚽ Antoine Griezmann made no secret of his admiration for CR7 following the announcement of his retirement from international football, praising the greatness of the Portuguese legend👀 Do you consider Cristiano Ronaldo the… pic.twitter.com/HjuIzDxi4k— beIN SPORTS USA (@beINSPORTSUSA) November 17, 2026 



A rivalry that started in LaLiga



Most of the duels between Ronaldo and Griezmann took place in LaLiga, where the Frenchman faced the Real Madrid star while wearing the colors of Real Sociedad and, later, Atletico Madrid. Their paths in Spain stopped crossing when Griezmann moved to Barcelona in 2019, since Ronaldo had already left Madrid for Juventus a year earlier.


        


The two also met at the international level, with the most memorable encounter coming in the Euro 2016 final. Portugal beat France in that match, and the victory gave Ronaldo the first major title of his career with the national team.



Their last meeting came on July 5, 2024, in the quarterfinals of Euro 2024. The match ended 0-0 after extra time, and Portugal advanced on penalties, closing the rivalry between two players who defined an era for their countries.



Griezmann’s words show the respect that remained between two players who spent years on opposite sides of some of football’s biggest stages. With Ronaldo gone from the international scene, Portugal now faces the challenge of moving forward without its all-time icon, while Griezmann continues his career in MLS with Orlando City.

items.title: Lionel Scaloni opens the door for Lionel Messi to join Argentina’s coaching staff for the 2030 World Cup
items.description:
Lionel Scaloni joked about a future role for Lionel Messi on Argentina’s bench, with an unexpected vacancy in the staff as the backdrop. 
Lionel Scaloni was asked about a scenario many Argentina fans have probably imagined since Lionel Messi retired from the national team: seeing the captain on the sidelines instead of on the pitch.



The head coach addressed it at the press conference ahead of the friendly against Costa Rica, the last match of the November international window, and his answer was a mix of humor and honesty.



Scaloni first made it clear that he doesn’t see Messi leaving the pitch anytime soon. “I think he’s going to keep playing. He’s going to keep playing beyond 2030. He already said no with the national team, but as a player, I hope he continues,” the coach said.



When the question turned to a possible role on the bench, Scaloni used the situation of Walter Samuel, who is leaving the staff after the Costa Rica match, to joke about it. “If he wants to come, there’s no problem. Now that Walter (Samuel) is gone, look… let him come,” he said with a smile.




👀🇦🇷 Lionel Scaloni on Leo Messi in the coaching staff for World Cup 2030: “I think Messi will still be playing football beyond 2030!”.“But now that Walter Samuel is leaving, he’s welcome whenever he wants”, he said smiling. 😁 pic.twitter.com/HSYmZo3pdB— Fabrizio Romano (@FabrizioRomano) November 17, 2026




Messi retired from the national team on Aug. 31, at 39, through a letter and a video that looked back at his career with the Albiceleste. His farewell in front of the home crowd came on Oct. 6 at the Monumental, in a 3-0 win over Benin in which he scored from the penalty spot and also assisted Nicolas Otamendi and Nicolas Paz. The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner leaves behind a huge legacy with 208 appearances, 126 goals and 67 assists, all of them records for Argentina.



Scaloni is confirmed for 2030 World Cup


        


Scaloni’s future was already settled before the comment about Messi. The Argentine Football Association announced on Nov. 12 that the coach extended his deal to lead the national team through the 2030 World Cup, with AFA president Claudio “Chiqui” Tapia presenting the news alongside him at a press conference. 



The agreement covers the 2027-2030 cycle and puts to rest the doubts about his continuity after Argentina fell to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final. The renewal also includes most of his staff, among them Pablo Aimar, who will remain through 2030 as well. The only exception is Samuel, who is leaving the setup to begin his own path as a head coach.



Scaloni’s new deal also puts him on course for a milestone no Argentine coach has reached. After guiding the team to the title in Qatar in 2022 and to the final in 2026, he will become the first Argentine manager to lead the national team in three different World Cups once the 2030 edition arrives.



For now, Messi’s name on the staff remains only a joke, and his focus appears to be on continuing as a player with Inter Miami. What is clear is that Scaloni will be on the bench through 2030, with the chance to keep writing his name in Argentina’s history book.

items.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation“Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes.The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. items.title: Canada vs Guatemala: Confirmed lineups for the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League match
items.description:
Take a look at the confirmed lineups for Canada vs Guatemala in the 2026-27 Concacaf Nations League. Canada and Guatemala meet again just days after their last meeting, with both camps naming unchanged-look lineups for the rematch in this Concacaf Nations League fixture.
Canada come into this one off a 3-2 win over this same Guatemala side on November 14, a result that showed they can get the job done even when they do not shut the door defensively. That match also marked their most recent outing, so Mauro Biello’s group will look to carry the same attacking edge into this second meeting. Another result here would keep Canada’s momentum rolling in this Nations League cycle.
Guatemala head into this match on the back of a 2-3 loss to Canada on November 14, a game in which they scored twice but still came up short. Before that, they had beaten Suriname 1-0 on October 6, showing they can grind out low-scoring wins when needed. Luis Fernando Tena’s side will be looking to flip the script against the same opponent and respond with a better result this time.
Canada confirmed lineup
Canada line up in a 4-4-2 with Maxime Crépeau behind a back line of Niko Sigur, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman and Richie Laryea. Mathieu Choinière and Nathan Saliba sit in midfield alongside wide options Tajon Buchanan and Liam Millar, giving Biello’s side width and the ability to get bodies forward quickly. Jonathan David partners Tani Oluwaseyi up front, pairing David’s finishing with Oluwaseyi’s movement. There are no absences to account for, so Canada field what looks like their strongest available group.
Canada confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Maxime Crépeau, Niko Sigur, Richie Laryea, Mathieu Choinière, Luc De Fougerolles, Joel Waterman, Tajon Buchanan, Nathan Saliba, Tani Oluwaseyi, Jonathan David, Liam Millar. Coach: Mauro Biello.
Guatemala confirmed lineup
Guatemala also set up in a 4-4-2, with Kenderson Navarro in goal protected by Aarón Herrera, Nicolás Samayoa, Allen Yanes and José Morales across the back. Rodrigo Saravia and José Rosales anchor the midfield while Óscar Santis and Jesús López provide width to support the front line. Rubio Rubín and Jehú Fajardo lead the attack, with Tena asking his front two to work off service from the flanks. With no absences listed, Guatemala are able to pick from a full squad for this rematch.
Guatemala confirmed starting XI (4-4-2): Kenderson Navarro, Aarón Herrera, José Morales, Rodrigo Saravia, Allen Yanes, Nicolás Samayoa, Óscar Santis, José Rosales, Rubio Rubín, Jehú Fajardo, Jesús López. Coach: Luis Fernando Tena.
